name: Google Colab

modes.label: On-demand
modes.note: Consumer Colab is billed in compute units at $0.0999/CU (US, $9.99 per 100 CU). Google does not publish per-runtime CU burn rates (shown live only in the resource monitor), so this mode is unpriced.

modes.label: Colab Enterprise (GCP, us-central1)
modes.note: E2 rates incl. 20% management fee (N1/N2/A2: 0.0379332/vCPU-h, 0.0050844/GiB-h). GPU per GPU-hour on top of the VM. Every runtime has a mandatory 100 GiB SSD boot disk ($0.000279452/GiB-h = $0.0279/h = ~$20.4/month) plus a data disk (default 100 GiB pd-standard $0.000065753/GiB-h), both billed while shut down. Default runtime e2-standard-4, idle shutdown 180 min (10-1440 min configurable or off), default runtimes auto-deleted 18 h after creation. Savings plans: 1-yr -10%, 3-yr -20%.

plans.name: Public rate not established
plans.note: Unknown limits are not promises of unlimited capacity.

plans.name: Google AI plans (Pro/Ultra)
plans.note: Eligible paid Google AI plans include a monthly CU allotment (amount not published on pages checked), premium GPUs and background execution on higher plans; CU from AI plan and Colab Pro add to one balance. EU prices seen: AI Pro 21,99 EUR/month, Ultra from 99,99 EUR/month.

free.note: GCP new-customer $300 credit applies to Colab Enterprise only; consumer Colab free tier has no dollar credit.

caveats: Notebook execution backend discovered inDatalayer code-sandboxes; not a provisioned general-purpose sandbox API. Free/Pro/Pro+ hardware capacity andcomputeunit economics are not arbitrary4/8 VM-hours.
Not fully priceable in ENGINE_CARD: unknown USD resource rates or machine shape. Null is not zero; do not rank as a free provider.

Features set to null were not verified. No sandbox was purchased or tested; feature/performance statements are documentation claims. Null maximums are unknown unless a cited note explicitly states unlimited.
A complete monthly bill requires known snapshot/egress/plan limits; do not silently treat missing ancillary charges as free.

Consumer Colab plans (US, 2026-09-27): Free $0 (no guaranteed GPU, 12 h max); Pay As You Go $9.99 per 100 compute units or $49.99 per 500 (EU EUR 11.10 / 50.70); Colab Pro $9.99/month = 100 CU; Colab Pro+ $49.99/month = 600 CU with background execution up to 24 h. CU expire after 90 days, non-refundable. Per-runtime CU burn rates are unpublished, so consumer Colab stays unpriced; plans not encoded because included CU would wrongly discount the Colab Enterprise mode.

fleet.default_max_instances: Consumer: unpublished; Enterprise: Compute Engine quotas + 60 runtime create/LRO requests per minute
fleet.tiers: Paid Colab plans improve resource access, but CPU/GPU/session limits remain dynamic and unpublished. Guaranteed resources require separate Google Cloud/Colab Enterprise or own runtime.
fleet.notes: Official FAQ explicitly does not publish fixed usage/availability limits; no defensible 10/50/300/1,000 fleet entitlement. Notebook limits, idle termination and prohibited-use restrictions make this unlike unrestricted VM hosting. Paid compute units are not a reservation. No fixed time-to-raise or numerical new GPU allowance published.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: While runtimes are shut down: Compute charges aren't generated because there isn't any CPU or GPU usage. Boot disk and data disk storage is charged.
snapshot_auto.note: Colab Enterprise idle shutdown (default 180 min, 10-1440 or off) stops the VM and keeps only its boot + data persistent disks (persistent disk, not a checkpoint; kernel/memory state lost). Default runtimes are deleted 18 h after creation with files lost. Consumer Colab: 'Virtual machines are deleted when idle for a while, and have a maximum lifetime' (FAQ) - nothing saved except notebooks in Drive.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: notebookRuntimes methods: start, get, delete, list, upgrade, stop, assign
snapshot_on_demand.note: Colab Enterprise runtime API has no snapshot/checkpoint/clone method; reuse is via runtime templates (config only, not state). Underlying GCE disks are Google-managed (not exposed in the user project as documented). Consumer Colab: no snapshot feature documented; users re-run install cells ('it's a good idea to include cells which install and load any custom libraries' - FAQ).

harness_api.quote: notebookRuntimes methods: start, get, delete, list, upgrade, stop, assign
harness_api.note: Gemini in Colab / Data Science Agent are UI features in the notebook; no public API to prompt them or stream their events. notebookExecutionJobs runs a whole notebook headless (not an agent harness). The Colab MCP server lets an external agent drive a Colab notebook (opposite direction). Claude Code/Codex etc. can only be run via notebook cells/terminal.

egress_allowlist.quote: In the Subnetwork menu, select a subnetwork. To turn off public internet access, clear Enable public internet access .
egress_allowlist.note: Colab Enterprise only: per runtime template choose VPC network/subnetwork, disable public internet (NetworkSpec.enableInternetAccess), and set Compute Engine networkTags so VPC firewall egress rules (IP/CIDR/port) apply; VPC Service Controls perimeter for Google APIs ('runtimes are subject to the service perimeter'). Domain-level (FQDN) filtering would need separate GCP products (Cloud NGFW / Secure Web Proxy) - not documented for Colab. Consumer Colab: no egress controls.

ingress_rules.quote: runtimeUser : Required. The user email of the NotebookRuntime.
ingress_rules.note: Colab Enterprise runtimes are single-user (assigned to runtimeUser) and reached only through an authenticated Google proxy (proxyUri, DATALAB_TUNNEL_TOKEN cookie) with IAM; runtime templates carry networkTags so VPC firewall ingress rules apply; no public URL per port. Consumer Colab port forwarding (google.colab.output.serve_kernel_port_as_iframe/window): 'The URL will only be valid for the current user while the notebook is open in Colab.' (colabtools _util.py). No public/shareable port URLs first-party.

secret_proxy.quote: Gets the model proxy token from user secrets or environment variables.
secret_proxy.note: Consumer Colab only: google.colab.ai calls Gemini (and other listed models) through Colab's model proxy service (MODEL_PROXY_HOST, OpenAI-compatible) with a Colab-issued MODEL_PROXY_API_KEY in the runtime, so no provider API key is needed in the notebook - a platform LLM gateway, and the proxy token itself is present in the runtime. User secrets (Colab Secrets, google.colab.userdata.get) are returned in plaintext to the kernel - not a proxy. Colab Enterprise: end-user credentials / ADC via the runtime identity, no credential-injecting proxy. No non-HTTP coverage.

volume_attach.quote: dataPersistentDiskSpec : Optional. The specification of persistent disk attached to the runtime as data disk storage.
volume_attach.note: Colab Enterprise: a data persistent disk (type + size set in the runtime template, default 100 GiB pd-standard) in addition to the fixed 100 GiB SSD boot disk; lives and dies with the runtime ('Boot disks and data disks are deleted when the runtimes are deleted'), not independently re-attachable. Consumer Colab: Google Drive FUSE mount (drive.mount(mountpoint, ..., readonly=False)); FAQ: 'Google Drive mounting on the runtime filesystem will not work' on Colab Enterprise/GCP Marketplace runtimes.

isolation.quote: Each runtime is a Compute Engine virtual machine that hosts your notebook execution.
isolation.note: Colab Enterprise runtimes are Compute Engine VMs (KVM-based); consumer Colab is 'a virtual machine private to your account' (FAQ) on the same GCE infrastructure. Derived, not an explicit hypervisor disclosure.

image_oci.note: Runtime templates select a fixed Colab-managed image release (e.g. Python version) via colab_image.release_name; there is no field to supply an arbitrary Docker/OCI image for the runtime itself.

nested_virt.quote: Colaboratory, or 'Colab' for short, is a product from Google Research that allows anyone to write and execute arbitrary Python code through the browser.
nested_virt.note: Not documented; Colab is a managed notebook execution environment, not a general VM API, and no /dev/kvm-in-guest capability is advertised. Not offered: outside the product's scope.

desktop.quote: remote control such as SSH shells, remote desktops ... bypassing the notebook UI to interact primarily via a web UI
desktop.note: Remote desktop access is explicitly listed among disallowed/restricted usage patterns and is not a first-party feature; Colab exposes only the notebook UI. Not offered: outside the product's scope.

browser.quote: Colaboratory, or 'Colab' for short, is a product from Google Research that allows anyone to write and execute arbitrary Python code through the browser.
browser.note: No managed/real browser instance is provided inside the runtime; users would have to install one themselves. Not offered: outside the product's scope.

computer_use.quote: Colaboratory, or 'Colab' for short, is a product from Google Research that allows anyone to write and execute arbitrary Python code through the browser.
computer_use.note: No screenshot+click API is offered. Not offered: outside the product's scope.

anti_bot.quote: Colaboratory, or 'Colab' for short, is a product from Google Research that allows anyone to write and execute arbitrary Python code through the browser.
anti_bot.note: Colab is a hosted notebook/compute product, not a browsing/automation product; no stealth/fingerprinting feature exists. Not offered: outside the product's scope.

captcha_solving.quote: Colaboratory, or 'Colab' for short, is a product from Google Research that allows anyone to write and execute arbitrary Python code through the browser.
captcha_solving.note: Not offered: outside the product's scope (notebook execution environment, not a web-automation/CAPTCHA product).

egress_ip_type.quote: In the Subnetwork menu, select a subnetwork. To turn off public internet access, clear Enable public internet access.
egress_ip_type.note: Runtimes egress through standard GCP datacenter IP ranges (default internet gateway / customer-configured Cloud NAT); no residential/mobile IP option exists.

snapshot.quote: While runtimes are shut down: Compute charges aren't generated because there isn't any CPU or GPU usage. Boot disk and data disk storage is charged.
snapshot.note: Only persistent disks survive stop/idle-shutdown (filesystem, not a snapshot artifact); no snapshot/checkpoint API exists (confirmed no snapshot method in the notebookRuntimes API), and no memory-state restore is offered.

fork.quote: notebookRuntimes methods: start, get, delete, list, upgrade, stop, assign
fork.note: No clone/fork method exists for runtimes; reuse is only via runtime templates (config, not machine state).

fork_running.quote: notebookRuntimes methods: start, get, delete, list, upgrade, stop, assign
fork_running.note: No clone capability at all, so cloning a running machine is not possible.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: notebookRuntimes methods: start, get, delete, list, upgrade, stop, assign
memory_snapshot_fork.note: No fork feature exists at all, so memory-preserving forks are not possible.

pause_resume.quote: notebookRuntimes methods: start, get, delete, list, upgrade, stop, assign
pause_resume.note: Colab Enterprise runtimes can be stopped and started (stop/start API + UI), and idle shutdown stops the VM automatically; compute billing stops while stopped, only disk storage is billed. Consumer Colab VMs are recycled rather than explicitly paused.

wake_on_request.quote: Idle shutdown Colab Enterprise enables idle shutdown by default.
wake_on_request.note: Idle shutdown stops the runtime, but nothing wakes it automatically on an incoming request; a user/API call must explicitly start it again.

persistent_disk.quote: Boot disk and data disk storage is charged.
persistent_disk.note: Boot + data persistent disks survive stop/idle-shutdown (billed while stopped) and are only deleted when the runtime itself is deleted (default templates auto-delete runtimes 18h after creation).

volume_shared.quote: dataPersistentDiskSpec: Optional. The specification of persistent disk attached to the runtime as data disk storage.
volume_shared.note: Data/boot persistent disks are attached to a single runtime each; no documented mechanism to mount one volume across multiple concurrently-running runtimes.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Colab Enterprise enables idle shutdown by default. This ... before shutdown, or you can disable idle shutdown.
auto_stop_idle.note: Default idle timeout ~180 min (configurable 10-1440 min or off); consumer Colab: 'Virtual machines are deleted when idle for a while' (FAQ).

max_session_h.quote: In the version of Colab that is free of charge notebooks can run for at most 12 hours ... Colab Pro+ supports continuous code execution for up to 24 hours if you have sufficient compute units.
max_session_h.note: Consumer Colab: free/Pro/Pay-As-You-Go ~12h max, Pro+ up to 24h with active execution; no hard guaranteed cap is published (varies by usage/availability). Colab Enterprise (the priced mode) instead auto-deletes default runtimes 18h after creation and stops for idle, but a running/actively-used session has no published fixed hour cap other than the 18h default template lifetime.

live_resize.note: Machine type/GPU is fixed by the runtime template used to create a runtime; changing shape requires creating a new runtime from a (new) template, not a live in-place resize of a running machine.

agent_harnesses.quote: notebookRuntimes methods: start, get, delete, list, upgrade, stop, assign
agent_harnesses.note: No coding-agent templates (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, etc.) are preinstalled or offered; only Colab's own Gemini-in-Colab / Data Science Agent UI assistant exists, and only as a UI feature, not a preinstalled third-party harness.

own_agent_api.quote: notebookRuntimes methods: start, get, delete, list, upgrade, stop, assign
own_agent_api.note: Gemini in Colab / Data Science Agent is a UI-only assistant with no public API to prompt it, stream its events, or drive it programmatically; notebookExecutionJobs only runs a whole notebook headless, it does not drive an agent.

lang_python.quote: Colaboratory, or 'Colab' for short, is a product from Google Research that allows anyone to write and execute arbitrary Python code through the browser.
lang_python.note: Colab is a Python-first Jupyter notebook environment with Python preinstalled by default.

lang_node.quote: Colaboratory, or 'Colab' for short, is a product from Google Research that allows anyone to write and execute arbitrary Python code through the browser.
lang_node.note: Node.js is not preinstalled/offered out of the box; a user would have to apt-get install it themselves inside a cell.

public_ipv4.quote: runtimeUser: Required. The user email of the NotebookRuntime.
public_ipv4.note: Colab Enterprise runtimes are reached only via an authenticated Google proxy (proxyUri), not a per-machine public IPv4; consumer Colab has no exposed IP at all.

inbound_https.quote: The URL will only be valid for the current user while the notebook is open in Colab.
inbound_https.note: google.colab.output.serve_kernel_port_as_iframe/window creates a temporary authenticated HTTPS URL to reach a port on the runtime; Colab Enterprise similarly exposes the notebook only via an authenticated proxyUri HTTPS URL. Scoped/private, not a general public ingress feature.

egress_http_rules.quote: In the Subnetwork menu, select a subnetwork. To turn off public internet access, clear Enable public internet access.
egress_http_rules.note: Egress control is at the VPC/IP/network-tag level (Compute Engine firewall rules) only; there is no HTTP method/path-level egress control documented.

guest_firewall.quote: remote control such as SSH shells, remote desktops ... bypassing the notebook UI to interact primarily via a web UI
guest_firewall.note: Colab notebooks are not documented as giving full root/kernel-level control needed to reliably manage nftables/iptables inside the runtime; root access itself is undocumented/unclear, so this is not confirmed as available (derived, low certainty of full VM-style guest network stack control).

static_egress_ip.quote: In the Subnetwork menu, select a subnetwork.
static_egress_ip.note: No first-party fixed outbound IP feature is documented for Colab; a customer could configure their own Cloud NAT with a static IP on their VPC but that is a general GCP networking feature, not a Colab product feature.

windows.quote: Each runtime is a Compute Engine virtual machine that hosts your notebook execution.
windows.note: Not offered: outside the product's scope. Colab runtimes use Colab-managed Linux images (colab_image release_name); no Windows machine option is documented.

macos.quote: Each runtime is a Compute Engine virtual machine that hosts your notebook execution.
macos.note: Not offered: outside the product's scope. Google Cloud/Colab does not offer macOS machines.

arm64.note: Documented example/available machine families are x86 Compute Engine types (E2/N1/N2/A2); no Arm-based (Tau T2A) machine type is documented for Colab Enterprise, and consumer Colab does not expose machine-type choice at all.

self_host.quote: Colaboratory, or 'Colab' for short, is a product from Google Research that allows anyone to write and execute arbitrary Python code through the browser.
self_host.note: Colab is a Google-hosted SaaS product; there is no distributable software to self-host. Not offered: outside the product's scope.

byoc.quote: Each runtime is a Compute Engine virtual machine that hosts your notebook execution.
byoc.note: Colab Enterprise runtimes run inside the customer's own GCP project/VPC (their own cloud account) for compute/networking, but the Colab control plane, proxy, and management service remain fully Google-operated SaaS rather than software deployed as a distinct managed instance into arbitrary customer infrastructure; not the self-serve 'deploy into your cloud' BYOC pattern documented for other providers.

open_source.quote: Colaboratory, or 'Colab' for short, is a product from Google Research that allows anyone to write and execute arbitrary Python code through the browser.
open_source.note: Colab itself (the notebook service, UI, and Colab Enterprise) is closed-source; only the underlying Jupyter format/some client libraries (colabtools) are open source, not the core product.

soc2.quote: Colab Enterprise Gemini in Colab Enterprise
soc2.note: Colab Enterprise is a listed Google Cloud Platform service governed by the standard GCP service terms/DPA; Google Cloud overall holds SOC 2 Type II attestation covering in-scope GCP services. Not independently itemized for consumer (free/Pro) Colab.

sso.quote: runtimeUser: Required. The user email of the NotebookRuntime.
sso.note: Colab Enterprise access is governed by Google Cloud IAM / the customer's Google Workspace or Cloud Identity, which supports SAML/OIDC SSO at the organization level; this is standard GCP identity federation, not a Colab-specific control.

eu_data_residency.note: Colab Enterprise runtimes/templates are created in a chosen Compute Engine region, and the card's own regions list includes 'eu'; customers can select EU regions to keep runtime data resident there. Consumer Colab has no region selection.

docker_inside.quote: The following are disallowed from all managed Colab runtimes: ... employing techniques such as containerization to circumvent anti-abuse policies
docker_inside.note: Colab's own FAQ explicitly forbids using containerization inside a managed runtime to work around its abuse/resource policies, and neither the consumer Colab FAQ nor the Colab Enterprise (Vertex AI notebookRuntimes) docs document Docker/OCI container support inside the runtime itself (custom container support is only for choosing the runtime's own base image, not for running a nested Docker daemon). Not offered/allowed as a supported feature.

hipaa.note: Google Cloud's HIPAA compliance page lists 'Colab Enterprise' (and 'Gemini in Colab Enterprise') among the Google Cloud services covered under the Google Cloud BAA, i.e. HIPAA-eligible when a customer has signed a BAA. This applies to Colab Enterprise (the GCP/Vertex AI product this card prices as its main mode); the free/consumer Colab product is not part of Google Cloud's BAA-covered service list.

ssh.quote: The following are disallowed from managed Colab runtimes running free of charge, without a positive Colab compute unit balance, and may be terminated at any time without warning: remote control such as SSH shells, remote desktops ... You can remove these types of restrictions by purchasing one of our paid plans ... and maintaining a positive compute unit balance.
ssh.note: reviewed: proposed correction rejected (Google's own FAQ confirms SSH shells into a Colab managed runtime are a real, working use case: it is only disallowed (and subject to termination) on the free-of-charge tier as an anti-abuse policy, and is explicitly an allowed activity once you hold a positive paid compute-unit balance. There is no native 'ssh user@host' connect string issued by Google (users self-host sshd/a tunnel such as ngrok or colab-ssh inside the notebook cell to reach it), so this is not a turnkey first-party SSH endpoint like a plain VM host, but the capability itself exists and is officially acknowledged/permitted, so the card's 'ssh: false' with no supporting evidence is wrong. Corrected value: true (paid plans; free tier risks termination for this use).)

usage_api.quote: Colab Enterprise runtimes run in your Google Cloud project and can be labeled with tags; costs are reportable via Cloud Billing API / BigQuery export filtered by resource labels and metadata.
usage_api.note: granularity: per-tag; cost: yes; Colab Enterprise (the paid GCP mode) supports per-runtime billing via GCP's standard Cloud Billing API and BigQuery export, which can be filtered by labels/tags set on notebookRuntimes. Consumer Colab (free/Pro) has no public API; CU burn rates are unpublished and only visible in the live resource monitor in the notebook UI. Medium confidence because the main consumer tier lacks an API.

persist_scope.quote: Boot disk and data disk storage is charged.
persist_scope.note: The whole disk survives a stop, installed packages included.
